question: What is the main job of the CSSD in a hospital?

options.B: Processing and sterilizing reusable medical equipment

explanation: The Central Sterilizing Supply Department (CSSD) is like the hospital's powerhouse for cleanliness! They clean, package, sterilize, and distribute all the medical tools used across the wards. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h1)

question: Why is the CSSD so important for infection control?

options.A: It breaks the chain of infection by providing sterile instruments
options.B: It administers routine vaccinations to hospital staff
options.C: It isolates patients with contagious airborne diseases
options.D: It monitors patient antibiotic resistance patterns daily

explanation: By making sure every tool is thoroughly decontaminated and germ-free, CSSD stops infections from spreading from one patient to another. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h1)

question: What kind of air pressure is kept in the CSSD washing and decontamination room?
explanation: Think of negative pressure like a vacuum that sucks air in. It pulls air into the room instead of blowing it out, keeping dirty germs trapped safely inside the washing area. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h2)

question: Why does the CSSD follow a strict one-way workflow?

options.A: To make it easier for staff to walk around the department
options.B: To ensure sterilizers are close to the main entrance
options.C: To prevent clean items from crossing paths with dirty items
options.D: To reduce the electricity consumed by heavy machinery

explanation: A one-way flow makes sure that freshly cleaned and sterilized supplies never bump into or cross paths with dirty instruments. Safety first! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h2)

question: What is the main use of an ultrasonic cleaner in the CSSD?

options.A: Killing bacterial spores using high heat
options.B: Removing microscopic debris using sound waves

explanation: Ultrasonic cleaners use high-frequency sound waves to create tiny scrubbing bubbles that blast hidden dirt out of tiny instrument hinges and joints. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h3)

question: Why must an instrument be properly cleaned before going into the autoclave?

options.A: Dried blood and tissue can block the sterilizing agent from reaching the surface
options.B: Remaining moisture causes the electrical elements to short-circuit
options.C: Organic dirt makes the metal too heavy for the sterilization tray
options.D: Dirty instruments will permanently stain the inside of the machine

explanation: If blood or tissue is left on a tool, it acts like a shield protecting the germs. The steam won't be able to reach them to kill them! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h3)

question: When should instruments be checked for cleanliness and damage?

options.A: Directly after removal from the autoclave
options.B: Only when the surgeon complains about a tool
options.C: As soon as the items arrive dirty from the ward

explanation: Staff inspect instruments right after they are washed and dried. This ensures no hidden dirt or broken parts slip through before they are wrapped up. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h4)

question: What is the most important feature of a good surgical instrument wrap?

options.A: It must change color to black when exposed to sunlight
options.B: It must completely block all air and moisture permanently
options.C: It must let the sterilizing agent in while blocking microbes
options.D: It must dissolve in water during the washing cycle

explanation: A good wrap has a clever design: it lets steam or gas pass through to clean the tools, but keeps tiny bacteria out after the process is done. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h4)

question: What is the most common and trusted way to sterilize metal surgical tools?

options.A: Boiling in water for twenty minutes
options.B: Steam under pressure in an autoclave
options.C: Ultraviolet radiation in a glass cabinet

explanation: The autoclave is the workhorse of the CSSD! Using high-pressure steam is fast, affordable, and extremely reliable for metal instruments. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h5)

question: Why must wrapped instrument trays be loaded loosely inside a steam sterilizer?

options.A: To allow steam to circulate freely around every package
options.B: To stop the external indicator tape from melting off
options.C: To prevent the heavy metal trays from breaking the door
options.D: To make unloading faster for the nursing assistant

explanation: If the packs are crammed too tightly together, the steam can't reach every surface, leaving pockets where germs can survive. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h5)

question: Which monitoring tool gives the absolute proof that bacterial spores have been killed?
explanation: Biological indicators use real, highly resistant harmless spores to test if the autoclave truly destroyed all living microorganisms. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h6)

question: What is the main limitation of a chemical indicator strip placed inside an instrument tray?

options.A: It can only be read using an ultraviolet microscope
options.B: It dissolves completely if the steam pressure gets too high
options.C: It only measures the external room temperature of the storage area
options.D: It shows that conditions for sterilization occurred, but not that spores are dead

explanation: Chemical strips change color when exposed to heat or steam, which proves the machine got hot enough. However, they don't test actual germ survival like biological tests do. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h6)

question: What stock rotation rule should be followed when storing sterile supplies?
explanation: Just like in a pharmacy or supermarket, 'First-In, First-Out' (FIFO) means older stock gets used first so nothing sits on the shelf long enough to expire. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h7)

question: Why is it important to let a hot sterilized pack cool down inside the autoclave before touching it?

options.A: Hot metal instruments will bend out of shape if exposed to room air
options.B: The packaging material will immediately catch fire if moved too quickly
options.C: Cooling down resets the chemical indicator strip color back to normal
options.D: Touching it while hot can draw moisture through the wrapper and contaminate the contents

explanation: Touching a hot, damp pack creates condensation. Water droplets act like an elevator for bacteria, letting them slip right through the wrapper! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h7)

question: What personal protective equipment is a must when working in the CSSD decontamination room?

options.A: Waterproof gowns, utility gloves, and face shields
options.B: Dust masks and cotton lab coats
options.C: Sterile surgical gloves and sterile cloth gowns only
options.D: Lead aprons and radiation dosimeter badges

explanation: Decontamination staff deal with splashes of dirty water, blood, and harsh chemicals, so waterproof gear and face shields are essential to stay safe. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h8)

question: What should you do immediately if you get a needle-stick injury from a used surgical tool?

options.A: Wait until the end of the shift before telling the supervisor
options.B: Wash the wound quickly and ignore it if there is no bleeding
options.C: Report the incident and follow the facility's post-exposure protocol
options.D: Soak the injured finger in strong chemical disinfectant

explanation: Never brush off a sharps injury! Report it right away so you can get quick medical checks and preventive care if needed. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h8)
